rules.quote: Address the Governor-General of Australia in the following style and order:
rules.violation_condition: The Governor-General’s full formal style omits required elements or places them in an order inconsistent with the specified sequence and incumbent-specific variations.
when: The text gives the Governor-General of Australia’s full formal style of address.
The base sequence is ‘His/Her Excellency the Honourable’, prefixed titles, given name and family name, post-nominals, then ‘Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia’.
Prefixed titles and post-nominals depend on those held by the incumbent.
A military rank goes before ‘the Honourable’.
‘Sir’ or ‘Dame’ goes after ‘the Honourable’.
The separately prescribed correspondence salutations are not full formal styles of address.
rules.why: G-2: the required sequence and incumbent-specific variations are one formal-style check.

examples.note: The plural is ‘governors-general’.

parts.quote: Australia has had 28 governors-general. A governor-general’s role is to represent the monarch.

rules.violation_condition: The plural of ‘governor-general’ is formed other than as ‘governors-general’, including leaving the noun singular when it refers to multiple holders.
when: The expression refers to two or more people who hold or have held the title.
Capitalisation is checked separately.
rules.why: The plural form is a different flag from the capitalisation requirement in the same sentence.

rules.quote: Address correspondence to the Governor-General to the Official Secretary at Government House, Canberra.
rules.violation_condition: Correspondence intended for the Governor-General lacks an address to the Official Secretary at Government House, Canberra.
when: The correspondence is intended for the Governor-General.
This concerns the delivery address, not the personal salutation.
rules.why: This specifies the correspondence recipient and destination, independently of title style and salutation.

covers.quote: To address the Governor-General personally in formal correspondence:
In less formal correspondence:
Open with ‘Dear Governor-General’.

rules.specification: The page does not define the boundary between formal and less formal correspondence. Determine or supply that classification before applying the corresponding opening.
rules.violation_condition: Correspondence addressed personally to the Governor-General lacks the opening appropriate to its formality: ‘Your Excellency’ for formal correspondence or ‘Dear Governor-General’ for less formal correspondence.
when: The Governor-General is addressed personally in correspondence.
Formal correspondence opens with ‘Your Excellency’.
Less formal correspondence opens with ‘Dear Governor-General’.
rules.why: G-2 combines the formal and less formal cases of one opening check; the closing is independently checkable.

covers.quote: To address the Governor-General personally in formal correspondence:
In less formal correspondence:

rules.specification: The page does not define the boundary between formal and less formal correspondence. Determine or supply that classification before applying the corresponding closing.
rules.violation_condition: Correspondence addressed personally to the Governor-General lacks the closing appropriate to its formality: ‘Yours faithfully’ for formal correspondence or ‘Yours sincerely’ for less formal correspondence.
when: The Governor-General is addressed personally in correspondence.
Formal correspondence concludes with ‘Yours faithfully’.
Less formal correspondence concludes with ‘Yours sincerely’.
rules.why: G-2 combines the formal and less formal cases of one closing check, separate from the opening.

covers.quote: For the partner of the Governor-General:
Address a male partner as ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Your Excellency’.

rules.quote: Address a female partner as ‘Her Excellency’ or ‘Your Excellency’.
rules.violation_condition: The Governor-General’s partner is addressed with a form other than the specified alternatives: ‘Her Excellency’ or ‘Your Excellency’ for a female partner, and ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Your Excellency’ for a male partner.
when: The person being addressed is the Governor-General’s partner.
For a female partner, either ‘Her Excellency’ or ‘Your Excellency’ is acceptable.
For a male partner, either ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Your Excellency’ is acceptable.
The page provides no further case.
rules.why: G-2: the female and male cases select acceptable forms for one partner-address check.
